roles._schemes: Three bar-mark schemes occur. Scheme A = H1-1..H1-10 (B=2.0m): two cycles, CYCLE-1 and CYCLE-2, each at 2x the face spacing (@300 for sp150, @250 for sp125), alternating. Scheme B = H1-11..H1-28: CYCLE-1, CYCLE-2,4, CYCLE-3, each at 4x the face spacing (@600/@500); CYCLE-3 is CYCLE-1 mirrored. Scheme C = H1-29..H1-50: same cycles as B, but the outer loop is split into L-shaped bars, so the marks are reassigned (T1/T2/T3, B1/B2/B3, T4-T6, B4-B6 change meaning; see below). The roles below are for scheme A (from H1-1) unless a scheme is named. Lengths in 'bars' are in m (the table prints values < 1 m in mm without a decimal point, e.g. 953 -> 0.953).
roles.T1: A: top slab outer (upper-face) main bar, one continuous ∩ bar over the full span and bent down into the outer face of both side walls (R=140 bends), CYCLE-1. B: same ∩ bar, CYCLE-1/3. C: one of the two L-shaped top outer bars (top-slab upper face plus the outer face of one wall), lapped near mid-span with T2, CYCLE-1/3
roles.T2: A/B: top slab inner (lower-face) main bar, straight over the full inner width between walls, CYCLE-1 (A) or CYCLE-1/3 (B). C: the second L-shaped top outer bar (upper face plus the other wall's outer face), CYCLE-1/3
roles.T3: A: top slab outer ∩ bar of CYCLE-2 (alternates with T1; slightly shorter legs into the walls). B: top-left outer corner L-bar (top slab upper face plus the upper part of the wall outer face), CYCLE-2,4. C: top slab inner (lower-face) full-width straight bar, CYCLE-1/3
roles.T4: A: short straight top slab inner (lower-face) mid-span bar, CYCLE-2. B: top-right outer corner L-bar, CYCLE-2,4 (mirror of T3). C: top-left outer corner L-bar, CYCLE-2,4
roles.T5: B only: short straight top slab inner (lower-face) mid-span bar, CYCLE-2,4. C: top-right outer corner L-bar, CYCLE-2,4
roles.T6: C only: short straight top slab inner (lower-face) mid-span bar, CYCLE-2,4
roles.B1: A/B: bottom slab inner (upper-face) main bar, straight over the full inner width, CYCLE-1 (A) or CYCLE-1/3 (B). C: same role, CYCLE-1/3
roles.B2: A/B: bottom slab outer (lower-face) main bar, one continuous ∪ bar bent up into the outer face of both walls, CYCLE-1 (A) or CYCLE-1/3 (B). C: one of the two L-shaped bottom outer bars (lower face plus one wall's outer face), lapped near mid-span with B3
roles.B3: A: bottom slab inner (upper-face) straight bar, CYCLE-2 (length = B). B: bottom slab inner (upper-face) straight bar, CYCLE-2,4. C: the second L-shaped bottom outer bar, CYCLE-1/3
roles.B4: A: bottom slab outer ∪ bar of CYCLE-2 (alternates with B2). B: bottom-left outer corner L-bar (lower face plus the lower part of the wall outer face), CYCLE-2,4. C: bottom slab inner (upper-face) straight bar, CYCLE-2,4
roles.B5: B: bottom-right outer corner L-bar, CYCLE-2,4. C: bottom-left outer corner L-bar, CYCLE-2,4
roles.B6: C only: bottom-right outer corner L-bar, CYCLE-2,4
roles.W1: Left side-wall inner-face vertical main bar, straight, CYCLE-1 (A) or CYCLE-1/3 (B, C) only. That is why the inner wall face is at twice the outer spacing (@300/@250). The outer wall face is formed by the legs of the T/B outer bars
roles.W2: Right side-wall inner-face vertical main bar (mirror of W1)
roles.H1: Haunch bar parallel to the 45° haunch at the two top inner corners: a straight part 'a' plus 135° bends with legs b=100. 2 per cycle, so N = 2 x cycles/m
roles.H2: Diagonal corner bar of the same shape as H1, at the two bottom inner corners (these corners are square, with no haunch)
roles.R1: Diagonal outer-corner bar: a straight part plus two b=300 legs bent at 135°. When R1 and R2 both appear, R1 is at the top outer corners. When only R1 appears (checked on H1-4, H1-11, H1-12), it is at the bottom outer corner. Appears from H1-4 onward, depending on load
roles.R2: Diagonal outer-corner bar like R1, at the bottom outer corners (when both R1 and R2 exist). In H1-11 and H1-16 the cycle 2,4 corner bar is the same as R1 and is merged into R1 with N=13.33
roles.R3: H1-50 only: additional diagonal bar (H19) at the bottom outer corners, placed next to R2
roles.D1: Top slab distribution bars (longitudinal, 배력철근), straight, L about 1.05-1.10 m per 1 m length including lap. N = number of bars across the top slab section (both faces)
roles.D2: Bottom slab distribution bars (longitudinal), straight, both faces
roles.D3: Side-wall distribution bars (longitudinal), straight, both walls and both faces
roles.S1: Shear/tie bar (⊓ shape: a = distance between the two mats, b=100 hooks) in the top slab, tying the upper and lower mats
roles.S2: Shear/tie bar (⊓ shape) in the bottom slab
roles.S3: Shear/tie bar (⊓ shape) in the side walls
